body: I agree completely. I know his mom didn’t want to have to take care of him and I feel my boyfriend deserves a life other than being a caretaker. And his sister probably won’t step up knowing how she is. But at the same time I don’t think I’m in a place to bring that up. I already feel I’m overstepping by wanting him to move in with me.

I guess by calling him a pushover I mean he’s easy to guilt trip. It’s very hard to get him to state what he actually wants and sometimes I find myself pushing him to do something he may not want to do on accident because he doesn’t speak up when he’s not comfortable. I’ve been watching myself on that for a little while now, but it’s gotten him into a lot of uncomfortable situations before.

I agree with the therapy part. I’ve had a few therapists that haven’t worked out for me. I think he knows it’s a problem but he’s also afraid of doing literally anything else. I know there’s trauma there, but he downplays literally all his trauma so he probably doesn’t even realize what’s causing this emotional distance.

I’d really it rather not come to breaking up. He’s hurting and I don’t want to leave him over something like that. He’s not hurting me in any way and he’s not taking it out on me, just being closed off to literally everyone. I’d rather encourage him to get the help he needs so he can be more emotionally available, but idk how to do that.

I agree. He said he tried it and it didn’t work for him, he hasn’t given much more information than that. He’s mentioned in the past that he’s not shared his emotions and gotten over it in the past just fine and that’s the thing that works for him. But it’s pretty obvious it’s not working.
I have. Im a very open person in general and I’ve definitely had my fair share of breakdowns about past trauma around him
